v.title: Who’s the Real European Striking Machine of the 2000s?
v.excerpt: BBC Sport’s fan poll crowns Messi as the top European striker of the century—Barcelona’s goal‑scoring legacy shines again.
v.body:
## Quick take
BBC Sport’s fan‑poll just dropped a definitive list of the top 10 European strikers of the century. Lionel Messi tops the chart, followed by a surprising mix of modern and classic names that remind us why the game has evolved.

## What happened
BBC Sport ran a nationwide poll across the UK, asking millions of football fans to vote for the best European striker of the last 20 years. The final tally was published on the BBC Sports site, and the results were shared across social media with a flurry of memes and debates. Messi, the Spanish forward who has dominated Barcelona’s attack for a decade, secured the top spot by a wide margin, while legends like Cristiano Ronaldo and Thierry Henry also made the list.

The article highlights the public’s preference for goal‑scoring prowess, pace, and technical skill. It also notes that the list is heavily skewed towards players who have been active in the Premier League or La Liga, reflecting the visibility of these leagues to the voting audience. A few surprises, such as Robert Lewandowski’s inclusion, show that the European football community still values modern clinical finishers.

## Why it matters
- **Barcelona’s identity**: Messi’s presence at the top of the list reinforces the club’s reputation as a breeding ground for world‑class strikers. It also suggests that future signings should aim to emulate his blend of playmaking and finishing.
- **Transfer market signals**: The inclusion of Lewandowski and other contemporary forwards indicates that clubs are looking for prolific scorers who can adapt to multiple leagues. This could influence the valuation of players like Erling Haaland or Kylian Mbappé.
- **Youth development**: The poll underscores the importance of nurturing talent from a young age. Barcelona’s La Masia could use this as a benchmark, focusing on developing players who can perform consistently across Europe’s top competitions.

## What’s next
Barcelona’s coaching staff will likely use this data to fine‑tune the offensive strategy for the upcoming season. Watching how the new striker—if any—fits into the team’s tactical setup will be crucial. Fans should keep an eye on the transfer window for any moves that could strengthen the front line, especially players who have proven themselves in both domestic and European competitions. The next chapter in Barcelona’s attacking evolution is about to begin, and the spotlight is on how the club responds to the expectations set by this fan‑driven ranking.

*Source: [The best European strikers this century - ranked by you](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cw5y1ver2rpyo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)*
